**Structuring collaboration features**

rounds.response: Proposed demo MVP scope: document list view, create/open/save with the existing rich-text editor core, real-time presence (avatars + live cursor positions) via current websockets layer, a right-hand comment panel (create/reply/resolve) but no inline comment popovers, and sharing strictly via the existing workspace sharing model. Out of scope for the demo: inline comments, any new permissions model, offline sync, and new infra changes. Acceptance criteria (all must be demoable with 3 concurrent users): 1) create/open/save a doc and persist edits; 2) concurrent edits from multiple users are reflected to others within 1s and merge without data loss; 3) presence shows avatars and live cursors for other editors; 4) comment panel can add/reply/resolve comments tied to a selection and display updates in real time; 5) sharing/permissions use the workspace model and a shared doc can be opened by invited teammates. Instrumentation: fire doc_open/doc_create/coedit_join/collab_start/comment_create/comment_resolve events and surface the three demo metrics (active docs w/>1 editor weekly, co-edit sessions per team, time-to-first-collaboration) in the demo dashboard. rounds.response:
Below is a compact story breakdown grouped as requested — each item shows Title — 1-line summary — Definition of Done — Tag (Must / Nice-to-have). 

Doc list cluster: 1) Document list view — show user’s docs, search, and open actions — DoD: list renders, search filters, opening a doc loads editor within acceptable band (<2s median), basic empty/error states; smoke test pass — Must. 2) Create / open / save flow — create new doc, persist edits via existing editor core — DoD: doc_create and doc_save flows create/persist records, doc_open loads with doc_id; manual save/auto-save demoable — Must (doc_* events: doc_create/doc_open/doc_save; dashboard: active docs metric). 3) Share via workspace model — expose existing share UI and open-by-invite — DoD: share flow uses current workspace sharing, invited user can open doc in demo; permission edge cases show friendly error — Must (doc_share event).

Editor + real-time cluster: 4) Editor integration — wire existing rich-text editor into docs surface, keyboard/formatting basics — DoD: formatting preserved across saves, unit tests for core behaviors — Must. 5) Real-time sync core — wire websockets-based diff/ops to sync edits between clients — DoD: concurrent edits from 3 demo users reflect within target bands (ideal <200ms / acceptable <1s), no data loss in smoke scenarios — Must (collab_*: coedit_start/coedit_end, client_latency_ms; supports co-edit sessions per team). 6) Presence UI (avatars + point cursors) — show who’s in doc and live cursor positions — DoD: avatars appear on join, cursors update in real time within target bands; visual treatment implemented for focused/idle states — Must. 7) Selection highlighting (cursor with selection) — show selection ranges vs point-only — DoD: if implemented, selections render and attribute to user; FLAG: fuzzy — confirm scope (point-only acceptable for demo) — Nice-to-have/fuzzy. 8) Merge/conflict simple policy & testing harness — basic last-write-merge behavior + scripted 3-client test — DoD: documented behavior, deterministic demo script showing merges; FLAG: may require discussion if deeper OT/CRDT needed — Must (for demo stability).

Comments cluster: 9) Right-hand comments panel (add/reply/resolve) — create comments tied to selection, show thread list, resolve behavior — DoD: comment_create/comment_resolve persist and propagate in real time, selection_range recorded, panel open/close interaction works, keyboard shortcuts basic — Must (comment_create/comment_resolve events with selection_range). 10) Comment UX states — unread indicator, anchor-to-selection on open, and error/loading states — DoD: visual unread badge, clicking thread jumps to selection, graceful failure UI — Must. 11) Inline comment popovers — show in-text anchors/popovers for comments — DoD: working popovers with create/reply — Nice-to-have (out of scope unless capacity).

Instrumentation & testing cluster: 12) Core telemetry implementation — implement doc_* and collab_* events with properties: doc_id, team_id, user_id, editor_count, session_id, session_duration_bucket, selection_range (where applicable), client_latency_ms, timestamp — DoD: events emitted for flows above, QA queries validate counts — Must (supports dashboard questions: # active docs with >1 editor, co-edit sessions per team, time-to-first-collab). 13) Demo dashboard panels & queries — create 3 demo widgets mapping to success metrics — DoD: working queries and visual widgets in staging dashboard showing live events during demo — Must. 14) Latency/load tests and verification — scripted test to measure edit-sync and list-load against ideal/acceptable bands — DoD: test runs with 3 concurrent clients and outputs latency distribution; test report added to spec — Must.

Design / UX tasks (callouts for Design Lead): 15) Visual spec for presence & cursors — define avatar size, colors, cursor labels, idle/focus states — DoD: final assets + component spec — Must. 16) Comments panel interaction design — open/close affordance, thread list layout, anchor behavior, unread state — DoD: annotated flows + microcopy — Must. 17) Loading/error states and empty states — list, doc load, real-time disconnect & reconnection UX — DoD: mockups + acceptance criteria — Must.

Open / fuzzy questions to resolve before sprint planning: confirm demo concurrency target = 3 users (assumed), decide whether selection highlighting is required or point-only cursors suffice, and finalize merge/conflict expectations (simple last-write merge vs stronger CRDT/OT). If you want, I can convert each story into Jira-style tickets with estimated points/hours after we confirm those three answers.

**Constructing demo sentences**

**Identifying demo dependencies and risks**

rounds.response:
Demo script (4 beats) — Beat 1: Create & share — user creates a doc and invites teammates (Doc list stories 1–3); Beat 2: Co‑edit live — invited users open and edit concurrently with editor + real‑time sync + presence visible (Editor/Real‑time stories 4–6); Beat 3: Comment & resolve — user opens RH comments panel, creates/replies/resolves a thread that propagates in real time (Comments stories 9–10); Beat 4: Leave & resume + metrics — users leave, later reopen from list and resume editing, and we surface live demo metrics on the staging dashboard (Doc list 1–3; Instrumentation/dashboard stories 12–13).  
Demo‑breaking dependencies/risks: real‑time sync core (5) + editor integration (4) + persistence (2) must be reliable together or co‑editing fails; share/invite (3) must grant access; comments propagation and selection_range persistence (9) are required for the commenting beat; failing instrumentation/dashboard (12–13) removes the ability to show success metrics.  
UX seams to flag: possible load/transition friction list→editor (need loading states), unclear affordance for opening/anchoring the RH comments panel, absence of inline popovers or selection highlighting (story 7) may confuse viewers, and last‑write merge behavior (story 8) can produce surprising results.  
Mitigations/decisions to lock for planning: confirm demo concurrency = 3 and accept point‑only cursors if selection highlighting isn’t ready; use scripted demo accounts and a pre‑populated doc to avoid cold starts; document/announce “last‑write wins” merge behavior in the script and defer inline comments as nice‑to‑have.

rounds.consequence: The succinct demo outline and list of demo‑breaking risks give the team enough clarity to finalize the sprint backlog quickly. In the planning meeting, they agree to constrain demo concurrency, explicitly defer inline comments, and add a small buffer story to harden the share/invite and real‑time sync paths so the narrative is less likely to fail live.

rounds.response:
Below is a concise click‑by‑click runbook (actions + suggested phrasing) followed by demo limitations.  
Step 1 — Create: start on Documents list, click "New Document", name it "Demo Plan" and open the editor; say "I'll create a shared doc that our small team can edit together."  
Step 2 — Invite & join: open Share, add demo_user_1 and demo_user_2, send invites, and have those scripted/demo accounts open the doc (or trigger them during the demo); say "Inviting teammates is immediate — they'll join and show up in the presence bar."  
Step 3 — Co‑edit, comment, leave/resume & metrics: with demo users typing simultaneously show live edits, avatars/cursors, then open the right‑hand comments panel, select text, add/reply/resolve a thread, close the doc, reopen from the list to show persistence, and open the staging dashboard to show active co‑edit sessions updating live; say "You can see edits and comments sync in real time, persistence when you come back, and the demo metrics updating on the dashboard."
